Hi Olivia — thanks for the report and the screenshot. Sorry for the disruption. Short answers up front:

- This impacted requests routed to our hosted cluster in us-west-2 and a subset of requests that were still using your shared hosted routing (not your Dedicated pool).
- Short-term mitigations you can try immediately (no infra changes required):
  * Temporarily disable streaming on your chat endpoint (poll for completion instead) — reduces head-of-line blocking and will avoid partial-response pauses.
  * Lower max_tokens on user-originated requests to 512 (helps the model finish faster and reduces queueing).
  * Set client-side streaming_heartbeat (send a small keepalive every 8s) — avoids connection timeouts while we stabilize.

We are investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline and permanent mitigations. I'll loop in engineering and send a concise post-incident note with suggested permanent fixes.

If you want, we can open a quick 30-min bridge to walk through steps now — say the next 30 minutes?

—Marcus

Subject: RE: PayGro incident — triage and actions (internal)

Quick technical summary and actions taken:

What happened (prelim):
- At ~23:47Z a small percentage of long-context streaming requests triggered KV-cache invalidations and forced cache re-materialization. That caused the serving runtime to fall back to slow off-path execution kernels for affected shards.
- Continuous-batching combined multiple streaming sessions into larger effective batches; a few long-lived streams created head-of-line blocking and increased tail latency across the batched set.

Mitigations applied (15 Jan 03:15Z):
- Temporarily disabled continuous-batching for streaming requests in the impacted host pool for tenant-tag:paygro-hosted.
- Forced prefix-cache warm for PayGro recent prompts (replay small sample load).
- Tuned the batch-slicer to cap per-session batch window to 80ms for streaming (was 200ms).

Customer-facing effects: reduced token arrival pauses from ~6–10s to sub-second for requests falling back to non-batched execution. Streaming still has slightly higher variance for long contexts; recommended customer actions align with Marcus' suggestions.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Full root-cause write-up (Sergio) — due 2026-01-16 18:00Z.
- Postmortem doc & customer summary (Marcus/Grace) — due 2026-01-16 20:00Z.
- Upgrade plan: add per-tenant continuous-batching controls and improve cache rematerialization path (infra epic).

Attachments: paygro_incident_timeline_20260116.pdf (timeline), streaming_mitigation_playbook_v1.md (runbook)

— Sergio

Subject: Post-incident follow-up: PayGro live chat latency (summary + action items)

Hi Olivia / PayGro team —

Thank you again for the quick reports and patience while we investigated. Attached is a short timeline and a small mitigation playbook. Below are the salient points and recommended next steps you can apply immediately and mid-term.

What we observed
- Impact window: 2026-01-14 23:47Z — 2026-01-15 00:27Z (peak between 23:50Z–00:10Z).
- Symptom: intermittent multi-second pauses in streaming token delivery followed by bursts; ~30% of active streaming sessions observed degraded token cadence.
- Root cause (prelim): interaction of continuous-batching with a small number of long-context streaming requests that triggered KV cache re-materialization and off-path kernel fallbacks, increasing tail latency for the whole batch.

Immediate mitigations we applied (already live)
- Disabled continuous-batching for streaming traffic tagged tenant:paygro-hosted (reduced head-of-line blocking).
- Warmed prefix cache and tuned batch-slicer cap to 80ms.
- Temporarily increased priority for small-token completions to reduce queue time.

Customer short-term actions you can take (no infra changes required)
- If you can tolerate slightly increased completion latency but smoother UX, switch to non-streaming (polling) mode for chat while we harden streaming; implementation: add ?stream=false on API calls or use the completion endpoint.
- Lower per-message max_tokens to 512 and break up very long prompts on the client side.
- Set a client-side streaming_heartbeat to keep connections alive (8s interval).
- If you have a Dedicated pool available, route high-volume traffic there; Dedicated pools avoid noisy-tenant interactions.

Mid-term recommendations
- We will add per-tenant continuous-batching controls so you can opt out of batching for streaming traffic.
- Improve KV cache rematerialization to avoid synchronous fallbacks.
- Add a streaming health-check metric stream (available in Redwood Console) to detect token-cadence degradation earlier.

Credits & next steps
- We're issuing a service credit for the affected window (details via your account team).
- I've attached the incident timeline and a short mitigation playbook you can apply immediately.
- If helpful, let's schedule a 45-minute readout with your eng and SRE teams next week to walk the timeline and remediation plan.

Attachments: paygro_incident_timeline_20260116.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — short chronology; streaming_mitigation_playbook_v1.md (markdown) — customer-facing steps and sample API toggles.

Status & postmortem

- Internal postmortem (editable): https://redwood.app/ops/postmortems/PG-3497-livechat-latency-20260116
